vLLM 0.31.0 | Freedom.Tech

 Release Mon, Oct 5, 2026 9 min read 

# vLLM 0.31.0

At a glance

VLLM 0.31.0 ships DeepSeek-V4.1 optimizations, weight-cache preload for fast restarts, speculative decoding on Model Runner V2, and large-scale serving improvements via expert parallelism and scheduling controls

Original release notes

## v0.31.0

## Highlights

This release features 717 commits from 307 contributors (96 new)!

- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash performance: FlashMLA mega attention with the V4.1 NVFP4 compressed KV cache is now the SM100 default (#56935); DeepGEMM sparse MQA logits for the indexer (#56254) and Mega-Gate fusing the gate GEMM with expert selection (#56266); decoder boundaries fuse the TP all-reduce, mHC input preparation (#57643) and the MoE finalize (#58586); a fused small-batch WO-A with inverse RoPE and MXFP8 quant on SM100/SM103 (#58634); the MXFP8 `wo_b` GEMM fused with the sequence-parallel reduce-scatter (#57428); Engram `wkv` sharded across TP ranks (#58678) and Engram host tables shared across co-located DP replicas by default (#57651); encoder CUDA graphs for the vision tower (#56625); and SWA bounded replay that keeps the sliding-window KV out of prefix caching (#56227).
- Fast restart: the new `vllm preload` CLI launches the weight-cache daemon that keeps post-quantized weights resident in GPU memory across engine restarts (#56680), now with data parallelism (#57386), MTP draft models (#57312), a `/health` endpoint (#58552) and a readiness wait (#58370). Experimental initialized-engine snapshots (`vllm snapshot create/restore`) use CRIU to restore a fully initialized TP1 engine (#51360).
- Model Runner V2 and speculative decoding: draft-model speculative decoding (#43091) and custom logits processors (#56497) on Model Runner V2; the new LiLiCorr drafter (#57934); async scheduling for DFlash (#58065) with the context K/V precompute captured in the draft CUDA graph (#57632); DSpark adaptive verification for Gemma4 (#57263) and variable-length decode for Kimi-K3 (#52988); a DCP target with a non-DCP DSpark draft (#56723); and MoE memory now counted during MRV2 profiling, avoiding OOMs on WideEP deployments (#57270, #58411).
- Large scale serving: MoonEP balanced EP all2all backend via `--all2all-backend moonep` (#52101), prefill context parallelism with data parallelism (#57075), a low-SM multimem reduce-scatter for SM100/SM103 (#55072), DeepEPv2 with sequence parallelism (#57210) and EPLB with shared-expert overlap (#57236), a sharding-aware NCCL M2N weight-transfer backend for RL (#51520), and KV offloading back-pressure detection (#50045).
- Scheduling controls: `--max-num-active-seqs` caps RUNNING admission independently of `max_num_seqs` (#56758), `--long-prefill-token-threshold` now adapts to the number of waiting prefills instead of chunking a lone request (#57951, #58459), the waiting queue was reworked so requests already holding KV blocks are scheduled first (#58947), and the KV connector + MTP deadlock under KV pressure was fixed (#57104).
- HiSparse hardening: MTP verification rows resolved with a union residency kernel (#59235), MTP acceptance collapse under FULL graphs fixed (#59309), no GPU pages without host backing (#59036), a chunked-prefill preemption livelock fixed (#59494), KV cache sized from the groups HiSparse allocates (#59450), and host prefix publication and GPU prefix adoption fixes (#59007, #59282).
- Security: per-request `mm_processor_kwargs` and `media_io_kwargs` are rejected unless `--trust-request-mm-kwargs` is set (#58830); prefix-cache extra keys are tagged by source so a LoRA name and a `cache_salt` can no longer collide (#51899), and the LoRA path is part of the block hash (#59335); stale multimodal receiver-cache entries can no longer replace fresh payloads (#57833).
- Breaking changes: per-request multimodal kwargs gated (#58830); `tokenizer_mode="slow"` removed (#58545); `--enable-mamba-fine-grained-prefix-cache` renamed to `--enable-mamba-shared-prefix-checkpoint`

results.text:
vLLM v0.31.0: 717 commits, `vllm preload` fast restarts, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash FlashMLA default, security gates and breaking changes — AICoder

Tooling· 9d ago

# vLLM v0.31.0: 717 commits, `vllm preload` fast restarts, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash FlashMLA default, security gates and breaking changes

vLLM Verified vllm-project

vLLM v0.31.0 (717 commits, 307 contributors, 96 new) adds the `vllm preload` weight-cache daemon for fast engine restarts and experimental CRIU engine snapshots, makes FlashMLA mega attention with NVFP4 compressed KV the SM100 default for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, brings draft-model speculative decoding to Model Runner V2, gates per-request multimodal kwargs behind a flag, and fixes prefix-cache key collisions between LoRA names and cache_salt. Several breaking changes ship too.

## Key Takeaways

- ✓ Scale: 717 commits from 307 contributors (96 new).
- ✓ Fast restart: `vllm preload` keeps post-quantized weights resident in GPU memory across restarts (DP, MTP drafts, /health); experimental CRIU snapshots restore an initialized TP1 engine.
- ✓ Security: per-request multimodal kwargs rejected unless `--trust-request-mm-kwargs`; LoRA path now part of the block hash to stop prefix-cache collisions.
- ✓ Breaking: `tokenizer_mode="slow"` removed; online `quantization="fp8"` replaced by `fp8_per_tensor`; `--enforce-eager` also disables JIT warmup.
- ✓ Model paths: GLM-5.3-Flash metadata ops 1.6–4.8x faster and 3 GiB indexer workspace saved; fused KimiViT QK RoPE up to 29x; ~25 s faster Qwen3.8-Flash-Next weight loading on DGX Spark.

### Key Decision Metrics at a Glance

TL;DR Verdict

vLLM Documentation docs.vllm.ai/

## In-Depth Technical Analysis

vLLM v0.31.0 (717 commits, 307 contributors) targets restart cost and multi-tenant safety. The new `vllm preload` daemon keeps post-quantized weights resident in GPU memory across engine restarts (with DP, MTP drafts, a /health endpoint and readiness wait), and experimental `vllm snapshot create/restore` uses CRIU to restore an initialized TP1 engine. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash now defaults to FlashMLA mega attention with NVFP4 compressed KV on SM100; Model Runner V2 gains draft-model speculative decoding and custom logits processors; `--max-num-active-seqs` caps running admission. Security: per-request multimodal kwargs are rejected unless `--trust-request-mm-kwargs` is set, and LoRA names/paths can no longer collide with cache_salt in prefix-cache keys. No end-to-end throughput headline was published; component numbers include 1.6–4.8x faster GLM-5.3-Flash metadata ops, up to 29x fused KimiViT RoPE, and ~25 s faster Qwen3.8-Flash-Next loading on DGX Spark. Breaking changes: `tokenizer_mode="slow"` removed, online FP8 via `fp8_per_tensor`, renamed Mamba prefix-cache flag, `--enforce-eager` also disables JIT warmup. Install with `pip install vllm` or `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.31.0`.

Up Next vLLM v0.30.0 ships 762 commits with hot paths for Kimi K3, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next

results.title: Request-controlled mm_processor_kwargs.code_revision allows remote code execution · Advisory · vllm-project/vllm · GitHub
results.text:
Request-controlled mm_processor_kwargs.code_revision allows remote code execution · Advisory · vllm-project/vllm · GitHub

jperezdealgaba published GHSA-h3rc-6mm3-gc2m

Oct 6, 2026

## Package

 vllm (pip) 

## Affected versions

>= 0.7.3, < 0.31.0

## Patched versions

>= 0.31.0

## Summary

An untrusted multimodal request can set `mm_processor_kwargs.code_revision`. When vLLM serves a model whose Hugging Face processor uses dynamic `auto_map` code and the operator enabled `--trust-remote-code`, this request value reaches `AutoProcessor.from_pretrained` and selects the Python revision imported by Transformers.

This lets a client replace the operator-reviewed processor module with code from another revision of the same model repository. The operator-selected model/data `revision` remains pinned; only the executed processor code changes.

Importing a Python module is arbitrary code execution in the vLLM API/renderer process. The PoC below demonstrates this with an import-time filesystem write. It is fully offline and does not require a GPU, model weights, or changes to a real Hub repository.

## Affected snapshot

- Repository: `vllm-project/vllm`
- Verified commit: `570735520942b6428ae98f1eb442c6d88adae55e`
- Verified with Transformers 5.15.0 and 5.16.1
- Affected release range has not been bisected

## Affected configuration

The vulnerable path exists when all of the following are true:

1. The served model's processor uses dynamic `auto_map.AutoProcessor` code.
2. The operator enabled `trust_remote_code`.
3. The server can fetch the request-selected revision, or it is already cached.
4. The attacker can create or otherwise control a revision in the served model repository. An example is a Hugging Face community pull-request ref when that repository permits them.
5. A multimodal request reaches the processor path.

The default `trust_remote_code=False` configuration is not affected.

## Attack surface

`mm_processor_kwargs` is accepted directly by public request models:

- `TokenizeChatRequest.mm_processor_kwargs`
- `ChatCompletionRequest.mm_processor_kwargs`

`/tokenize` is particularly relevant because vLLM's authentication middleware guards only `/v1`, `/v2`, `/inference`, and `/cohere` prefixes:

- `AuthenticationMiddleware`

Consequently, `/tokenize` remains unauthenticated even when `--api-key` is configured, unless an external proxy protects it. The vLLM Security Guide documents `/tokenize` as an unprotected endpoint.

## Root cause

The request value follows this path:

1. `OnlineRenderer.preprocess_chat` places request `mm_processor_kwargs` in prompt extras.
2. Multimodal rendering forwards those kwargs into processor construction through `MMProcessorInputs` and `_process_multimodal_async`.
3. `MultiModalConfig.merge_mm_processor_kwargs` overlays inference values on startup values, so the request wins.
4. `cached_get_processor_without_dynamic_kwargs` filters only recognized processor-call keys. `code_revision` is retained as a processor-construction kwarg.
5. `cached_processor_from_config` pins `revision` and `trust_remote_code`, but forwards the remaining kwargs without reserving `code_revision`.
6. `get_processor` calls `AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(..., revision=revision, trust_remote_code=trust_remote_code, **kwargs)`.
7. Transformers `AutoProcessor.from_pretrained` uses `code_revision` to retrieve and import the dynamic module through `get_class_from_dynamic_module`, then removes it before loading processor data. This is why code comes from the attacker revision while configuration/data remain operator-pinned.

Request-time processor arguments are not separated from processor-construction arguments, and `code_revision` is not reserved.

## Security impact

- Confidentiality: High
- Integrity: High
- Availability: High
- Execution context: vLLM API/renderer process

Suggested CVSS v3.1: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` = 9.8 Critical

This Base score assumes the affected configuration described a

- Site A — EXIF `ImageID` multimodal alias: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H` (6.5, Moderate)
- Site B — untyped prefix-cache extra keys: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N` (3.1, Low)
- CWE: CWE-807 (Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision), CWE-345 (Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity), CWE-284 (Improper Access Control)

## Affected

- Ecosystem / package: pip / `vllm`
- Affected versions: vLLM ≤ 0.25.1 (confirmed on 0.25.1, commit `752a3a504485`). The lower bound predates 0.25.1; maintainers can confirm how far back each cache-key derivation reaches.

## Summary

vLLM keys shared cross-request caches on values that a caller can control or influence, without binding those values to a principal or to the actual media content. Two distinct caches are affected by the same root cause — cache identity is derived from a caller-controllable value with insufficient binding/namespacing, so a chosen or forged value aliases another request's shared cache state.

1. Site A — EXIF `ImageID` becomes the multimodal cache key. The multimodal hasher treats a UUID-valued EXIF `ImageID` as the entire hash input for an image. Two visually different request images that carry the same EXIF UUID therefore produce the same multimodal hash, and the processor cache returns the first request's cached item for the second. Ordinary requests are supposed to be keyed on actual content; only the explicit `multi_modal_uuids` interface is meant to carry caller-chosen identity.
2. Site B — untyped prefix-cache extra keys collide across domains. The prefix-cache block-hash builder flattens LoRA name, multimodal hashes, first-block `cache_salt`, and prompt-embed hashes into a single untyped tuple. Because the domains are not tagged, equal strings from different fields collide: a request under static LoRA `foo` and a base-model request with `cache_salt="foo"` both yield first-block `extra_keys = ("foo",)` and the identical `BlockHash`. KV state produced under a LoRA can then be served to a base request (or vice-versa), defeating the documented `cache_salt` isolation guarantee. The effect is confined to the first block, because `cache_salt` is injected only at `start_token_idx == 0` while the LoRA name persists on every block, so chained hashes diverge after block 0.

Prefix caching is enabled by default (`enable_prefix_caching=True`), and the multimodal processor cache is on the default multimodal path; neither site requires an opt-in feature.

Both sites are distinct from published fixes in the same areas: Site A survives GHSA-c65p-x677-fgj6 (whose fix adds image size/mode/info to `tobytes()` serialization) because the EXIF-`ImageID`→hash branch short-circuits before content is serialized and returns caller-supplied UUID bytes; Site B survives GHSA-rm76-4mrf-v9r8 (CVE-2025-25183, which seeds `hash()` to remove predictability) because this is a preimage collision from untyped domain keys that yields identical hashes regardless of seed or hash algorithm.

## Affected code

Links pinned to the confirmed commit `752a3a504485` (v0.25.1).

Site A — EXIF `ImageID` multimodal cache alias:

- The hasher returns `ImageID.bytes` instead of image content when EXIF contains a UUID: `vllm/multimodal/hasher.py#L52` (`serialize_item`) and `vllm/multimodal/hasher.py#L154` (`hash_kwargs`).
- That value becomes the processor-cache

vLLM 0.31 Upgrade Notes: Preload and Breaking Flags

# vLLM v0.31.0 Upgrade Notes: Preload Daemon, CRIU Snapshots, CUDA 13 Default and the Breaking Changes

Owen Park AI security researcher · Published Oct 13, 2026, 9:35 AM EDT

vLLM 0.31.0 adds a preload daemon and CRIU snapshots, moves the default build to CUDA 13.0, and removes or renames flags. What to check before upgrading.

vLLM v0.31.0 shipped on 5 October 2026 with 717 commits from 307 contributors, 96 of them new. It adds a weight-cache daemon for faster restarts, experimental CRIU snapshots and new scheduler controls. It also makes CUDA 13.0 the default build and removes several quantization and tokenizer options. Anyone who runs vLLM in production or pins its flags in deployment manifests should read the breaking changes before upgrading. This follows our v0.30.0 upgrade notes.

## What is new

Fast restarts with `vllm preload`. The new CLI starts a daemon that keeps post-quantized weights in GPU memory across engine restarts (#56680). Follow-ups add data parallelism (#57386), MTP draft models (#57312), a `/health` endpoint (#58552) and a readiness wait (#58370). ModelOpt MXFP8 pre-processed weights are also supported (#57316).

Experimental CRIU snapshots. `vllm snapshot create` and `vllm snapshot restore` save and restore a fully initialized TP1 engine using CRIU (#51360). It is marked experimental, so keep it out of production paths for now.

Scheduling flags.

- `--max-num-active-seqs` caps RUNNING admission separately from `max_num_seqs` (#56758).
- `--long-prefill-token-threshold` now scales with the number of waiting prefills, so it no longer chunks a lone request (#57951, #58459).
- The waiting queue was reworked so requests that already hold KV blocks are scheduled first, replacing `skipped_waiting` (#58947).
- A KV connector and MTP deadlock under KV pressure is fixed (#57104).

CUDA 13 by default. `pip install vllm` and the `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.31.0` image now target CUDA 13.0. CUDA 12.9 remains available as `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.31.0-cu129` and as CUDA 12.9 wheels for x86_64 and arm64. With uv, use `uv pip install vllm --torch-backend=auto`. CPU and XPU wheels are also published.

vllm preload keeps weights resident across engine restarts; CRIU snapshots are experimental and TP1 only. Source: vLLM release notes.

## Breaking changes to check

- `quantization="fp8"` now redirects to the `fp8_per_tensor` online shorthand (#53585). Check that this matches your accuracy and memory expectations.
- Quark silent online quantization is removed. Use the online quantization API (#51800).
- The AllSpark INT8 W8A16 backend is removed (#58001).
- `tokenizer_mode="slow"` is removed (#58545). Under Transformers v5 it already behaved like `"hf"`, so switch to `"hf"`.
- Per-request `mm_processor_kwargs` and `media_io_kwargs` are rejected unless the server starts with `--trust-request-mm-kwargs` (#58830). Server-level flags and offline `LLM` are unaffected.
- `--enable-mamba-fine-grained-prefix-cache` is now `--enable-mamba-shared-prefix-checkpoint` (#57382).
- `--enforce-eager` now also disables JIT kernel warmup, unless fault tolerance is enabled (#58197, #58593).
- `VLLM_XPU_ENABLE_XPU_GRAPH` is removed; XPU graphs are on by default (#51600). `VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD` is removed; use `--engram-config` (#57937).

## Security hardening

Prefix-cache extra keys are now tagged by source, and the LoRA path is part of the block hash (#51899, #59335). The release notes do not describe an attack. The change narrows what different requests can share in a prefix cache. The new `--trust-request-mm-kwargs` gate also stops clients from passing processor options to a server that did not opt in.

## What defenders and operators should do

1. Check your driver and container base against CUDA 13.0. If you cannot move, pin the `-cu129` image or wheels.
2. Search configs and launch scripts for the removed and renamed flags and variables listed above.
3. If clients send per-request multimoda

# vLLM v0.31.0: Major Serving Improvements, Speculative Decoding, and Breaking Changes

vLLM v0.31.0 introduces speculative decoding, broader model support, significant serving performance upgrades, and major API changes including deprecations and new defaults. Developers using vLLM for large model inference or multimodal workloads must review breaking changes and new features.

October 5, 2026 · Oct 5

## What changed?

vLLM v0.31.0 is a major release with over 700 commits, introducing several serving performance upgrades, speculative decoding capabilities, extended model and multimodal support, and important breaking changes in configuration and API behavior.

 Source: github.com

- Speculative decoding support using draft models, including LiLiCorr drafter and custom logits processors.
- Fast restart support: post-quantized weights can remain on GPU across engine restarts via `vllm preload`.
- Large-scale serving enhancements: sharded weight transfer, all2all communication backend, improved admission scheduling, and parallelism features.
- Expanded model coverage: optimized paths for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, GLM-5.3-Flash, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, Kimi K3, MiniMax-M3, and others.
- More multimodal types supported and processing improved with new kernels.
- Scheduler controls improved with new flags and better queue handling.
- BREAKING: Gating of per-request multimodal kwargs—now requires `--trust-request-mm-kwargs`.
- BREAKING: Removed features and renamed flags (e.g., `tokenizer_mode="slow"` removed, quantization shorthand, backend removals).
- BREAKING: XPU graphs are enabled by default and their environment variable removed.

## Why does it matter to an everyday developer?

These changes impact developers running LLM inference backends, particularly those supporting large deployments, multimodal inference, or custom workflows. The new speculative decoding allows much faster throughput when using LLMs that support draft-execute patterns. Large model and sequence handling is now more efficient and scalable with new serving infrastructure. Breaking changes can directly affect application behavior and deployment—especially if you use multimodal features or previously removed configuration options.

- Performance: Lower latency and higher throughput for draft model workflows and new parallelism features.
- Stability: Engine can now restart faster with GPU-cached weights.
- Security: Restricts risky per-request multimodal arguments by default.
- Compatibility: Some CLI flags and config options have been renamed or removed, requiring code or infra changes.

## What can the developer do now?

1. 1

#### Review and adapt to breaking changes

If using per-request multimodal kwargs, explicitly set `--trust-request-mm-kwargs`. Replace or remove any use of `tokenizer_mode="slow"`, online quantization `quantization="fp8"`, and related deprecated features. Update flag names like `--enable-mamba-fine-grained-prefix-cache` (now `--enable-mamba-shared-prefix-checkpoint`).
2. 2

#### Test speculative decoding

If using supported draft/execute model pairs (e.g., LiLiCorr), enable speculative decoding to improve inference throughput. Review model documentation for eligibility and required configuration.
3. 3

#### Leverage new serving infrastructure

Use features like fast restart (`vllm preload`), sequence parallelism, or new scheduling controls if you run high-availability or scaled clusters.
4. 4

#### Update deployment scripts and Docker images

Ensure Docker images, wheel installation, and environment variables match the new defaults (e.g., XPU graphs now default on).
5. 5

#### Review and test multimodal input handling

Check your pipelines if you process audio, video, or images—additional types and optimizations are available.

vLLM v0.31.0 introduces breaking changes. If your app relies on deprecated options or per-request kwargs, immediate attention is needed to avoid service disruption.
